title: Two-minute pulse: announcement + Q&A skeleton (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, scannable template for a 90–120s announcement segment followed by a 3–5 Qs rapid Q&A.
Used for: weekly all-hands slot, CEO/CTO 2-min drop-ins, or regional townhalls.
Notes to self: keep language crisp, avoid operational minutiae, list one explicit action for employees, include one data point (metric or date).

Structure (top-level) — 2 min announcement + live rapid Q&A (3–5 mins):
1) Opening line (10–12s): one-sentence framing. e.g. “Quick update: we’re rolling out X to stabilize latency in EU regions this week.”
2) What happened / what’s changing (30–40s): one short paragraph. bullet facts.
3) Why it matters (20–25s): concrete impact for customers or teams.
4) Ask / next steps (15–20s): what we want employees to do (if anything).
5) Where to learn more (10s): link to doc + channel.
6) Rapid Q&A (3–5 short questions): starters + suggested short answers, and escalation owner.

Draft wording (example) — keep this under 120s:
"Hi everyone — two quick items. First, we’re enabling the EU burst pool fallback for hosted API traffic starting tonight to reduce observed tail latency. Second, we’re putting a brief feature-flagged throttle on non-critical embedding jobs for twelve hours while we validate throughput metrics.
Why: the bursts keep customer requests within SLO during peak usage and the throttle avoids queue storms that spike costs.
If you run customer-facing flows, expect intermittent 503 fallbacks to dedicated variants for a short window; no action needed unless you own critical contracts (see list).
More: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/AB-rollback-playbook — join #ops-rapid if you see anything odd.
"

Rapid Q&A (scripted starters):
Q1: "Will customers see errors?"
A1: "Possibly brief fallbacks; all high-SLA customers are on dedicated pools — ops will DM owners for any exceptions. Escalation: Arjun S. (#ops-rapid)."

Q2: "How long is this change?"
A2: "Target window is 12 hours tonight; we’ll reassess metrics at T+6. If stable, we’ll release a short postmortem. Owner: SRE/Platform (Maya G.)."

Q3: "Are there cost implications?"
A3: "Short-term costs may rise due to fallback capacity; Optimize team will run cost-normalization after window. Internal action: finance flag ENG-2745. Owner: Product Ops."

Q4 (preemptive): "Will this impact private deployments?"
A4: "No — private/VPC customers run in their own infra. We’ll notify any partners if we identify cross-tenant impact. Owner: Solutions Eng. (poster note)."

Q5 (if time): "How can I help?"
A5: "If you’re on support rotation, skim #ops-rapid and have the fallback checklist ready. If you own a customer on the exception list, standby for an ops ping. Otherwise no action. Owner: oncall lead."

Open items / TODOs (personal):
- Confirm the exact list of exception customers with AE (Arjun to confirm by 2025-03-14 EOD).
- Attach brief one-pager with 'what to say to customers' for CS. (Draft in Confluence, needs review).
- Get an explicit SRE approval line for the all-hands script (Maya).
- Prepare lighting Qs for CEO drop-in: 2 factual, 1 takeaway.

Tone guide:
- Empathy first — lead with reassurance.
- Use active voice, short sentences.
- Call out what to do and what not to do.
- No deep technical detail in the spoken line; link to playbooks.

Slack anchors / where to post:
- Pre-announce to #team-leads 30m before all-hands.
- Post in #all-hands-announcements immediately after live.
- Pin confluence link in #ops-rapid.

Metrics to collect post-drop: (quick check list)
- Error rate (5xx) delta during window (Ops dashboard).
- Latency P95/P99 pre and post change (observability).
- Any customer tickets mentioning 'latency' or 'errors' in 24h.

Fallback lines for tricky live questions (one-liners):
- "We prioritized customer availability; this action reduces the risk of larger outages."
- "We’ll publish the findings and next steps within 48 hours."
- "If you see something you think is related, post in #ops-rapid with timestamp and we’ll triage."

Longer-term notes (should not be read live, for followup doc):
- Capture quick timeline and RCA stub for the all-hands followup.
- Consider adding a tiny customer-facing blurb if ticket volume increases.
- Evaluate whether Optimize rules can auto-suggest throttle thresholds in the future.

Draft checklist for finalizing before live: (tickbox-style)
- [ ] Confirm owner names + Slack handles correct
- [ ] Finalize example wording with CEO (two lines exactly)
- [ ] Post pre-brief in #team-leads 30m prior
- [ ] Have post-mortem skeleton ready in Confluence

Random scratch thoughts (keep or discard):
- Could do a 30s internal-only postmortem instead of a long doc — faster signal.
- If this recurs, create a short canned response for CS side.
- Consider an evergreen note in the weekly SRE newsletter with the 'why we throttle.'

End of scratchpad.
